item.title: Kakinoha-zushi: Nara's Persimmon-Leaf Sushi — Guide
item.description: Kakinoha-zushi is the signature sushi of landlocked Nara, especially the Yoshino mountains, and a clever solution to an old problem: with the sea far away, salted mackerel (and now salmon) was pressed with vinegared rice and wrapped in a persimmon leaf, whose natural antibacterial qualities preserved the fish and lent it a subtle aroma. The result is a neat, leaf-wrapped parcel of pressed sushi, unwrapped like a small gift, with a firm bite and clean, slightly tart flavour that keeps well — traditionally made for festivals and now a beloved everyday specialty sold in shops and stations across the prefecture.

item.title: Nara Food Guide: Kakinoha-zushi, Miwa Somen & Ancient Capital Cuisine
item.description: Nara’s food culture runs deeper than its understated reputation suggests. As Japan’s first permanent capital, Nara was the point of entry for Tang Chinese culinary techniques, Buddhist temple cooking, and the rice cultivation that would define Japanese cuisine. Today’s Nara specialities trace directly back to that heritage: pressed sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves for preservation, the oldest documented noodle tradition in Japan, and a sake-brewing lineage connected to the country’s most ancient shrine.
